About the Role

We are seeking a motivated and analytical ICT Business and Systems Analyst to join our growing team. In this role, you will work closely with business stakeholders to understand operational requirements, analyse existing systems, and deliver technology solutions that improve efficiency, productivity, and business performance.

You will act as the bridge between business needs and technical implementation by gathering requirements, documenting processes, and supporting the successful delivery of ICT projects.

Key Responsibilities

Consult with stakeholders to identify business needs and system requirements.
Analyse current business processes and recommend technology-driven improvements.
Gather, document and validate functional and technical requirements.
Prepare business requirement documents, process maps, user stories and functional specifications.
Work closely with software developers, project managers and third-party vendors to implement solutions.
Perform system testing, user acceptance testing (UAT) and quality assurance activities.
Assist with system integration, deployment and post-implementation support.
Analyse data and prepare reports to support business decision-making.
Develop user documentation, training materials and standard operating procedures.
Identify opportunities for process automation and digital transformation.
Monitor system performance and recommend ongoing improvements.
Ensure solutions comply with organisational policies, security requirements and industry best practices.

Skills & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Information Systems or a related discipline.
Minimum two years' experience as an ICT Business Analyst, Systems Analyst or similar role.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Experience gathering and documenting business requirements.
Knowledge of business process modelling techniques.
Experience with SQL, databases and reporting tools is desirable.
Understanding of SDLC, Agile and/or Waterfall methodologies.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
Strong documentation and presentation abilities.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently.
Desirable
Experience with ERP, CRM or enterprise software platforms.
Knowledge of Microsoft 365, Power BI or business intelligence tools.
Exposure to cloud technologies and API integrations.
Experience within digital transformation or software implementation projects.
What We Offer

Competitive salary package of $80k - 95k

Career development and professional growth opportunities.
Collaborative and supportive work environment.
Opportunity to work on innovative ICT and digital transformation projects.
Flexible working arrangements where applicable.

Cyber Security Analyst | SOC Operations, Threat Hunting & Vulnerability Management   Your new company     Join a well-established public sector organisation dedicated to delivering critical services across Western Australia. Operating within a modern technology and security environment, the organisation is focused on strengthening its cyber security posture through proactive monitoring, threat detection, risk management, and continuous improvement initiatives.    Your new role     
 As a Cyber Security Engineer / Analyst, you will play a key role in cyber security operations, supporting the monitoring, investigation, and response to security incidents across enterprise environments. Working within a security-focused team, you will contribute to threat intelligence activities, vulnerability management, security assessments, and ongoing security improvement programs. 
 Key responsibilities include: 
 
 Monitoring and analysing security events, alerts, and incidents. 
 Performing SOC activities including incident triage, investigation, and response. 
 Conducting threat hunting and threat intelligence analysis. 
 Supporting vulnerability assessments, security reviews, and audit activities. 
 Assisting with penetration testing and security validation exercises. 
 Performing security assessments of systems, applications, and cloud environments. 
 Preparing security reports, recommendations, and technical documentation. 
 Supporting compliance with cyber security frameworks, standards, and best practices. 
 
  What you'll need to succeed     
 To be successful in this role, you will possess: 
 
 Experience in Cyber Security Operations, SOC, or Security Analyst roles. 
 Strong incident detection, investigation, and response capabilities. 
 Hands-on experience with SIEM platforms such as Microsoft Sentinel. 
 Knowledge of vulnerability management tools and security assessment practices. 
 Understanding of threat intelligence, threat hunting, and indicators of compromise (IOCs). 
 Exposure to network security technologies including firewalls, IDS/IPS, VPNs, web proxies, and endpoint security solutions. 
 Knowledge of Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365 security services. 
 Familiarity with cyber security frameworks including ACSC Essential Eight, ISO 27001, NIST, and ISM. 
 Relevant tertiary qualifications in Cyber Security, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related discipline. 
 Industry certifications such as Security+, CEH, SC-200, AZ-500, CISSP, or equivalent will be highly regarded. 
 
  What you'll get in return     
 
 Competitive hourly contract opportunity. 
 Opportunity to work within a mature cyber security environment. 
 Exposure to modern security technologies and enterprise-scale security operations. 
 Collaborative and supportive technical team. 
 Valuable experience contributing to critical cyber security initiatives. 
 Free onsite parking and excellent workplace facilities.

JBS Australia is the largest and most respected meat and food producer in Australia. We have a strong portfolio of leading and renowned beef, lamb, pork, salmon and value-added branded products, such as AMH, Swift, Primo, Murray Valley and Huon. JBS Australia is a part of the global JBS business, the largest animal protein business in the world, and the second largest food company, with operations in North America, South America, Europe, Australia and New Zealand.

The JBS Dinmore Processing Plant is the largest beef facility in the southern hemisphere. Located near Ipswich, in south east Queensland, the facility has a daily production ability of 3,400 cattle and employs approximately 2,600 people. Cattle are sourced from the finest cattle producing regions to produce a diverse range of pasture fed and grain beef products, from commodity to premium. The renowned AMH brand, the award-winning Yardstick, the highly marbled grain fed Pure Prime and our state’s brand, Queenslander Beef and more are all produced at Dinmore.

About the Role:
We are currently seeking a Mechanical Engineering Technician to join our Dinmore Plant. We are seeking a passionate and energetic individual who is committed to the position and providing an effective professional service. This is a fantastic opportunity to join our dynamic, exciting organization who are the leaders in safety and culture across Australia. Within the role you will enjoy the benefits and satisfaction in contributing to the continued growth and success of our business. This role will be responsible for providing maintenance support to all areas across the plant to ensure the attainment of Production, Quality/FSQA, and Workplace Health and Safety requirements and objectives. This is a full-time position with the annual salary more than $79,423 plus superannuation.

Your key responsibilities will include:
Conducts tests of mechanical systems, collects and analyses data, and assembles and installs mechanical assemblies in support of Mechanical Engineers and Engineering Technologists.
Ensuring maximum equipment uptime is achieved by providing effective and efficient mechanical preventative and breakdown maintenance
Engaging in fabrication, installation and repair of mechanical machines, instruments or appliances
Ensuring that all work is carried out to the Company and requirements and conforms to all relevant regulations
Utilising fault-finding to troubleshoot and rectify problems

About you
Previous experience in a fast-paced industrial manufacturing environment
Previous experience within the meat industry advantageous
Sound knowledge of pneumatics and hydraulics, as well as a basic knowledge of electrics and welding skills
Excellent interpersonal skills
Demonstrated continuous improvement approach
Ability to support a broad variety of mechanical work
High level of accuracy and attention to detail
Ability to communicate at all levels
Ability to work autonomously as well as in a team environment
Ability to work various shifts
Full Australian working rights

Why work for us:
Retail discounts with national partners

Heavily discounted meat products

USVD Consultants Pty Ltd (ACN 666 075 065) ABN: 80 993 362 158 is a recruitment company having office at Bella Vista NSW 2153.

Our client Thinksupreme Pty Ltd (TSPL), ABN: 99 648 206 393 (Business name: Supreme Aluminium Windows) located at: Unit 3 78 Heathcote Rd Moorebank NSW 2170. Proudly Australian owned and operated for over 60 years, they have been Sydney's most trusted supplier of aluminium windows & doors. They manufacture a large range of residential and commercial windows and doors using top of the line materials and cutting-edge production technologies. They specialise in New Builds, Developments, Renovations, Office, Commercial or Industrial Windows & Doors.

Due to their business growth and expansion plans, USVD is now looking to recruit Machinist(s) in their Operations team on a permanent full-time basis.

Role: Machinist
No. of positions: Multiple, minimum 02
Reports to: Operations Supervisor
Location: Unit 3 78 Heathcote Rd MOOREBANK NSW 2170
Annual offered salary: AUD $82,000 - $88,000 base + Super (for a 38-hour work week)

Purpose of the role: We are seeking an experienced Machinist or may be two to join our operations team on a full-time basis. Set up and operate lathes, CNC, Milling, Grinding, Drilling & Turning machines to produce metal components to the specified tolerances, in accordance with technical drawings and safety requirements as per Australian standards.

As a Machinist, your main duties and responsibilities include:
•	Interpret engineering and technical drawings, sketches and specifications (including AS 1100/AS 1102 standards) to determine job requirements, tolerances and machining sequences.
•	Set up and operate lathes to perform turning operations, producing components to specified tolerances using a full range of lathe accessories.
•	Set and adjust computer-controlled (CNC) machines and processes, resolving technical difficulties.
•	Set up and operate milling machines to perform milling operations on components to required tolerances and specifications.
•	Set up and operate grinding machines to perform grinding operations and check finished components for conformance to specification. 
•	Set up and operate general workshop machines (drills, saws, etc.) for basic machining operations in a maintenance or jobbing environment.
•	Carry out mechanical cutting and holing operations using a range of cutting equipment.
•	Perform precision mechanical measurement, selecting and applying appropriate measuring instruments and interpreting results.
•	Perform general engineering measurements using mechanical measuring devices and visual inspection techniques. 
•	Use hand tools and portable/fixed power tools safely and correctly for a variety of general engineering tasks.
•	Use tools and equipment to manually produce components to precise dimensions and finishes on metallic and non-metallic materials.
•	Perform routine calculations, including percentages, ratios, proportions and averages, and interpret simple charts/graphs relevant to machining tasks.
•	Shut down and isolate machines and equipment safely in accordance with relevant Australian Standards and WHS legislation.
•	Carry out manual handling of materials and components in line with Safe Work Australia guidelines.
•	Operate fixed/moveable load-shifting equipment to move and position materials and stock.
•	Order and requisition materials, consumables and tooling as required for production and maintenance tasks.
•	Work safely with industrial chemicals, solvents, coolants and materials used in the machining environment.
•	Plan and prioritise daily work activities in line with established procedures and WHS policies.
•	Organise, record and communicate production, job and maintenance information using workplace systems (including computer-based systems). 
•	Participate in and contribute to environmentally sustainable work practices in the workshop.
•	Work effectively as part of a production/engineering team, contributing to team goals and quality outcomes.
•	Assist in providing on-the-job training and guidance to apprentices, trainees or other production staff.
•	Interpret technical specifications and equipment manuals to inform machining and maintenance decisions.
•	Comply with WHS procedures, quality systems and legislative requirements at all times.

Qualification & Licences:
•	Certificate III in Engineering - Mechanical Trade – Metal Machinist (First class) preferred.
•	At least 5 years of proven work experience in the above job role. 
•	Sound experience as Machinist in Metal fabrication environment. 
•	Well experienced of WHS requirements, particularly in manufacturing and steel fabrication environment. 
•	Ability to interpret technical drawings, manuals, and specifications.
Skills:
•	Strong organizational and time management skills 
•	Excellent attention to detail 
•	Ability to multitask and physically fit
•	Process and results driven 
•	Team player; collaborative 
•	Resilient, patient and adaptable 
•	Enthusiastic, self-motivated 
•	Proactive & hard-working

Additional information:
•	Ability to work outside of normal business hours on occasion when delivering key orders. 
•	Ability to travel interstate, if required.
